Implementation Plan

Issue #9765 plan: add the `[issue:N]` run-name to both clarify-respond wrappers. The planning ref is `orchestrator/project-9421` at `487acb290d67e0cf35b6abd0c9a7ed659a9e2470`, and the integration branch matches.

The `[E2E ` exception stays. The issue says to keep it only if a release-gate reader finds clarify-respond runs by issue title, and the gate's `"Clarif"` name match does exactly that (details in D1).

- `workflow-templates/ai-orchestrate-clarify-respond.yml`

- `changelog.d/9765-clarify-respond-run-name.md` (new)

   - The `display_title` reader audit result for clarify-respond (see "Testing considerations").
   - No `agents.md` edit and no new log prefix.

## Data structures affected
- The GitHub Actions run `display_title` of clarify-respond runs changes from the issue title to `<name> [issue:N]`. The only exception is issues whose title starts with `[E2E `, which keep the issue title.
- `ACTIVE_WORKFLOW_ISSUES` (output of `build_active_issue_set`) now also includes issues with only a queued or in-progress clarify-respond run. The poller code does not change.

## API or interface changes
- No new identifiers, env vars, log prefixes or API calls.
- The run titles of two workflows change. Consumers see this in the Actions UI after the next stable sync.

## Decisions
### D1 — Keep the `[E2E ` exception in both run-names
- Chosen: use the same `startsWith(github.event.issue.title, '[E2E ') && github.event.issue.title || format(...)` expression as the six Phase 3 wrappers.
- Alternatives considered: plain `format('<name> [issue:{0}]', github.event.issue.number)` without the exception.
- Why: the issue says to keep the exception only if a release-gate reader finds clarify-respond runs by issue title, and one does.
  - `find_latest_scoped_run_field` (`scripts/comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh` lines 218-260) selects runs with `.name | test($name_re; "i")` and `.display_title == $title`.
  - The gate calls it with `"Clarif"` (`test-and-mark-stable.yml` lines 1052, 1100, 1120, 5908), and that regex matches `AI Orchestrate Clarify Respond`.
  - Dropping the exception would change which runs the gate matches for smoke issues. Keeping it leaves gate behaviour byte-identical (§6 backward compatibility, §2 preserve behaviour). It also keeps the single parametrized contract test valid for all eight wrappers.

### D2 — Record the convention in a new `agents.d` fragment; leave the Phase 3 fragment alone
- Chosen: add `agents.d/9765-clarify-respond-run-name.md` that supersedes the deferral sentence.
- Alternatives considered: edit the deferral sentence in `agents.d/stuck-backlog-phase3-queue-backpressure.md` in place.
- Why: that fragment is also touched by open PR #9442, so an in-place edit risks a merge conflict. The issue also asks for "an `agents.d/` fragment that updates the run-name convention", and §25 prefers a new per-issue fragment.

### D3 — Add a poller-level linkage test for clarify-respond names
- Chosen: add one `_active_set` test with both the internal and the consumer clarify-respond names.
- Alternatives considered: rely only on the run-name string pin.
- Why: the acceptance criterion is about `ACTIVE_WORKFLOW_ISSUES` membership. The test costs about 15 lines and uses the existing harness ("Boil the Lake": the complete option is cheap).

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** `github.event.issue.title` is attacker-controllable, so it is used only as a run title, the same as today's default title. It is never interpolated into a `run:` shell body, so there is no new injection surface. `github.event.issue.number` is an integer the platform sets.
- **Forged tags:** `build_active_issue_set` links a run only when its event is `issues`/`issue_comment` and `display_title == name + " [issue:N]"` exactly, with N matching `^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$`. A pull-request title or an arbitrary issue title carrying `[issue:N]` cannot link a run.
- **`[E2E ` titles:** an issue titled `[E2E ...` falls back to the legacy untagged title, which is pre-change behaviour with no privilege gained (as the Phase 3 fragment already documents).
- **Unchanged:** no permissions, secrets, job `if:` predicates or authorization gates change, and the job-level trusted-author predicate is untouched.
- **Abuse case:** a non-collaborator comments to trigger a run. The job `if:` still skips it. A skipped run with a tagged title could be linked, but the six existing wrappers already have that property, and `workflow_run_is_fresh` and the zombie window bound it.

## Risks and edge cases
- **Conflict (snapshot vs issue text):** this workspace's copy of `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` (581,979 bytes, identical to `isolated-base`) shows `_issue_linked_run_matches(run, *, title, wanted)` without the `number=` tag
